stories.event: The US–Iran war continues with the Strait of Hormuz closed by the IRGC since 26 October and Iran's tanker blockade extended to the Gulf of Oman. On Sunday 25 October Qatari mediators delivered a letter from Vice President JD Vance to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei proposing a framework for negotiations and a meeting soon, led by Vance, possibly in Qatar or Türkiye; no date has been set. The New York Times reported the letter was well received and that Rezaei was expected to respond on Thursday 29 October; Iran has not commented publicly. Trump denies directing peace talks, and the Wall Street Journal reports he told Gulf allies to prepare for a short, intense campaign after the 3 November midterms. Foreign Minister Araghchi says Tehran is in close contact with mediators on its seven-day Hormuz plan.

stories.event: The ANO–SPD–Motoristé coalition's bill abolishing the ČT and ČRo licence fees (sněmovní tisk 231) passed first reading at 04:36 on Sat 24 Oct. It would fund ČT with CZK 5.74bn from the state budget (about 1bn below fee income) and ČRo with 2.065bn. Staff of both broadcasters (Veřejnoprávně) called a full-day strike for Tue 3 Nov, and students called a warning strike the same day. The drama unions at the National Theatre declared strike readiness on 27 Oct. On 29 Oct ČT director Hynek Chudárek told the Chamber media committee the cut would stop ČT working properly. He then met PM Babiš at 19:00, asking to keep funding at today's level, change the indexation and add guarantees of independence. No outcome had been published by 20:30. The coalition expects the second reading in January.

stories.event: On Thursday 29 October 2026 the ECB announced that President Christine Lagarde will step down on 7 February 2027, about nine months before her term ends (31 Oct 2027). The ECB said she had informed the Governing Council and European Council President António Costa. Costa said the procedure to appoint her successor was being launched the same day. The successor is appointed by the European Council under Article 283 TFEU, after a Eurogroup/Council recommendation, with at least 16 euro-area states representing 65% of the population behind it. Former Dutch central bank governor Klaas Knot (backed by The Hague) and BIS chief and former Bank of Spain governor Pablo Hernández de Cos (backed by Madrid) are seen as the front-runners. The Eurogroup next meets on 9 November.

stories.event: The ANO–SPD–Motoristé coalition passed an amendment over a Senate veto (19 Aug) and President Petr Pavel's veto. It strips the President of the power to appoint and recall heads of permanent missions to international organisations and gives it to the foreign minister. The change is one of about 80 amendments linked to the civil service act and can apply from 1 Nov 2026. On Fri 23 Oct, 38 senators and more than 50 opposition deputies asked the Constitutional Court to annul it and to consider an interim measure because of 'nebezpečí z prodlení'. By the evening of 29 Oct the Court had published nothing on the petition. In June the Court granted the President an interim measure within two days in a separate competence dispute over the NATO summit (Pl. ÚS 16/26).

stories.event: Ahead of the 3 Nov 2026 US midterms, the Justice Department sued California and Los Angeles County on 15 Oct to force the sequestration of mail ballots of about 20,000 people it alleges are noncitizens. On 26 Oct a Ninth Circuit panel (Bennett, Sanchez; Bumatay dissenting) dismissed its premature appeal (No. 26-7070) for lack of jurisdiction. Two judges said they would also deny on the merits. On 28 Oct Judge David Carter (C.D. Cal., No. 2:26-cv-12025-DOC-ADS) denied the emergency request, writing 'These threats must stop.' The department filed a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit within about two hours. The department has made a similar demand for 405 ballots in Washington state.
